jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]電車[でんしゃ]{で|de-means}会社[かいしゃ]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: I go to the office by train every morning.
why: The vehicle you travel by takes で.

jp: 駅[えき]{から|kara-from}空港[くうこう]{まで|made-until}バス{で|de-means}四十分[よんじゅっぷん]かかります。
en: It takes forty minutes by bus from the station to the airport.
why: The starting point of a trip takes から; まで marks the end point.

jp: この電車[でんしゃ]{は|wa-topic}京都[きょうと]{まで|made-until}止[と]まりません。
en: This train does not stop until Kyoto.
why: まで marks the point up to which a state or action continues: no stops until Kyoto.

jp: 新幹線[しんかんせん]{は|wa-topic}バス{より|yori-comparison}ずっと速[はや]いです{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: The Shinkansen is much faster than the bus, isn't it?
why: The thing you compare against is marked with より: faster than the bus.

jp: この電車[でんしゃ]{は|wa-topic}空港[くうこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きません。
en: This train does not go to the airport.
why: The place a train goes to is the destination of 行く and takes に or へ.

jp: 切符[きっぷ]{は/が|wa-topic}駅[えき]{で|de-place}買[か]えます。
en: You can buy tickets at the station.
why: Buying is an action carried out at a place, so the place takes で.

jp: 友達[ともだち]{と|to-with}京都[きょうと]{へ/に|ni-destination}旅行[りょこう]{に|ni-purpose}行[い]きました。
en: I went on a trip to Kyoto with a friend.
why: A companion who does the action together with you takes と.

jp: 公園[こうえん]{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{の|no-possessive}道[みち]{を|o-path}まっすぐ歩[ある]いてください。
en: Please walk straight along the road in front of the park.
why: The road you move along is marked with を.

jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]七時[しちじ]{に|ni-time}家[いえ]{を|o-departure}出[で]ます。
en: I leave home at seven every morning.
why: The place you leave with 出る is marked with を.

jp: 新宿[しんじゅく]{で|de-place}電車[でんしゃ]{を|o-departure}降[お]りました。
en: I got off the train at Shinjuku.
why: The vehicle you get off with 降りる is marked with を.

jp: 駅[えき]{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{に|ni-location}銀行[ぎんこう]{が/は|ga-existence}あります。
en: There is a bank in front of the station.
why: あります says something exists in a place, and the place of existence takes に.

jp: あの角[かど]{に|ni-location}郵便局[ゆうびんきょく]{が/は|ga-existence}あります{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: There is a post office at that corner.
why: The thing whose existence is stated with あります takes が, not を.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}東京[とうきょう]{で|de-place}雨[あめ]{が|ga-subject}降[ふ]っています。
en: It is raining in Tokyo today.
why: Rain is the subject doing the falling, so it takes が.

jp: どの電車[でんしゃ]{が|ga-question}空港[くうこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きます{か|ka-question}。
en: Which train goes to the airport?
why: A question word that is the subject takes が.

jp: 次[つぎ]{の|no-possessive}電車[でんしゃ]{は|wa-topic}何時[なんじ]です{か|ka-question}。
en: What time is the next train?
why: A sentence-final か turns the sentence into a question.

jp: 駅[えき]{は|wa-topic}今日[きょう]人[ひと]{が|ga-subject}多[おお]いです{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: The station is crowded today, isn't it?
why: ね asks the listener to agree with what you both can see.

jp: 空港[くうこう]{で|de-place}お土産[みやげ]{と|to-and}お茶[ちゃ]{を|o-object}買[か]いました。
en: I bought souvenirs and tea at the airport.
why: と joins two nouns of the same kind into one list: souvenirs and tea.

jp: これ{は|wa-topic}私[わたし]{の|no-possessive}切符[きっぷ]です。
en: This is my ticket.
why: の links the owner to the thing owned: my ticket.

jp: あの人[ひと]{は|wa-topic}ホテル{の|no-possessive}人[ひと]です。
en: That person works at the hotel.
why: の links the hotel to the person belonging to it: a hotel person.

jp: 先生[せんせい]{の|no-possessive}家[いえ]{は|wa-topic}駅[えき]{の|no-possessive}近[ちか]く{に|ni-location}あります。
en: My teacher's house is near the station.
why: の links the owner to the thing owned: the teacher's house.

jp: 友達[ともだち]{は|wa-topic}京都[きょうと]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きました。私[わたし]{も|mo-also}行[い]きました。
en: My friend went to Kyoto. I went too.
why: も adds a second person to what was just said: I went too.

jp: 電車[でんしゃ]{は|wa-topic}九時[くじ]{に|ni-time}駅[えき]{に|ni-destination}着[つ]きます。
en: The train arrives at the station at nine.
why: A clock time you can point to takes に.

jp: 新幹線[しんかんせん]{は|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]六時[ろくじ]{に|ni-time}東京[とうきょう]{を/から|o-departure}出[で]ます。
en: The Shinkansen leaves Tokyo at six every morning.
why: A clock time you can point to takes に.

jp: 京都[きょうと]{へ/に|ni-destination}お寺[てら]{を|o-object}見[み]{に|ni-purpose}行[い]きます。
en: I am going to Kyoto to see the temples.
why: The stem of a verb plus に before a movement verb states the purpose of going.

jp: 空港[くうこう]{へ/に|ni-destination}友達[ともだち]{を|o-object}迎[むか]え{に|ni-purpose}行[い]きます。
en: I am going to the airport to pick up a friend.
why: The stem of a verb plus に before a movement verb states the purpose of going.

jp: 駅[えき]{で|de-place}友達[ともだち]{を|o-object}待[ま]ちました。
en: I waited for my friend at the station.
why: The person you wait for is the direct object of 待つ and takes を.

jp: 昨日[きのう]電車[でんしゃ]{の|no-possessive}中[なか]{で|de-place}切符[きっぷ]{を|o-object}なくしました。
en: Yesterday I lost my ticket on the train.
why: The thing you lose is the direct object of なくす and takes を.

jp: 空港[くうこう]{まで/に|made-until}電車[でんしゃ]{で|de-means}行[い]けます{か|ka-question}。
en: Can I get to the airport by train?
why: A sentence-final か turns the sentence into a question.

jp: そのバス{は|wa-topic}空港[くうこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きません{よ|yo-assertion}。
en: That bus doesn't go to the airport, just so you know.
why: よ tells the listener something they probably do not know yet.

jp: 昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]{は|wa-topic}駅[えき]{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{の|no-possessive}店[みせ]{で|de-place}食[た]べました。
en: I ate lunch at the shop in front of the station.
why: Eating is an action carried out at a place, so the place takes で.

jp: 空港[くうこう]{は/が|wa-topic}駅[えき]{から|kara-from}遠[とお]いです{か|ka-question}。
en: Is the airport far from the station?
why: The thing you are asking about is the topic of the sentence and takes は.

jp: ホテル{は|wa-topic}駅[えき]{から/に|kara-from}近[ちか]いです。
en: The hotel is close to the station.
why: から marks the point you measure the distance from.

jp: 母[はは]{と|to-with}電車[でんしゃ]{で|de-means}買[か]い物[もの]{に|ni-purpose}行[い]きました。
en: I went shopping with my mother by train.
why: A companion who does the action together with you takes と.

jp: 日曜日[にちようび]{に|ni-time}家族[かぞく]{と|to-with}動物園[どうぶつえん]{へ/に|ni-destination}行[い]きました。
en: On Sunday I went to the zoo with my family.
why: The people who go together with you take と.

jp: 来週[らいしゅう]{の|no-possessive}月曜日[げつようび]{に|ni-time}新幹線[しんかんせん]{で|de-means}大阪[おおさか]{へ/に|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: I am going to Osaka by Shinkansen next Monday.
why: A day you can point to takes に.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}毎朝[まいあさ]八時[はちじ]{の|no-possessive}バス{に|ni-target}乗[の]ります。
en: My older brother takes the eight o'clock bus every morning.
why: The vehicle you get on is the target of 乗る and takes に.

jp: 駅[えき]{で|de-place}先生[せんせい]{に/と|ni-target}会[あ]いました。
en: I met my teacher at the station.
why: The person you meet is the target of 会う and takes に or と, never を.

jp: 一週間[いっしゅうかん]{に|ni-frequency}二回[にかい]、電車[でんしゃ]{で|de-means}大阪[おおさか]{へ/に|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: Twice a week I go to Osaka by train.
why: A unit of time plus に before a count says how often per that unit.

jp: 駅[えき]{に|ni-location}外国[がいこく]{の|no-possessive}人[ひと]{が/は|ga-existence}たくさんいます。
en: There are many foreigners at the station.
why: The people whose presence is stated with います take が, not を.

jp: この道[みち]{は|wa-topic}とても静[しず]かです{ね|ne-agreement}。
en: This street is very quiet, isn't it?
why: The thing being described is the topic of the sentence and takes は.

jp: 昨日[きのう]{の|no-possessive}電車[でんしゃ]{は/が|wa-topic}とても混[こ]んでいました。
en: Yesterday's train was very crowded.
why: The thing being described is the topic of the sentence and takes は.

jp: 母[はは]{に|ni-recipient}京都[きょうと]{の|no-possessive}お土産[みやげ]{を|o-object}あげました。
en: I gave my mother a souvenir from Kyoto.
why: The person who receives something you give takes に.

jp: 駅[えき]{の|no-possessive}人[ひと]{に/から|ni-source}道[みち]{を|o-object}聞[き]きました。
en: I asked someone at the station for directions.
why: The person you ask something is the source of the information and takes に.

jp: 大阪[おおさか]{まで|made-until}新幹線[しんかんせん]{で|de-means}二時間[にじかん]です。
en: It is two hours to Osaka by Shinkansen.
why: The vehicle you travel by takes で.

jp: 明日[あした]{は|wa-topic}どこ{へ/に|ni-destination}行[い]きます{か|ka-question}。
en: Where are you going tomorrow?
why: The place you go to with 行く is the destination and takes へ or に.

jp: あの店[みせ]{で|de-place}新[あたら]しい地図[ちず]{を|o-object}買[か]いました。
en: I bought a new map at that shop.
why: Buying is an action carried out at a place, so the place takes で.

jp: この近[ちか]く{に|ni-location}トイレ{が/は|ga-existence}あります{か|ka-question}。
en: Is there a restroom near here?
why: A sentence-final か turns the sentence into a question.

jp: 朝[あさ]九時[くじ]{から|kara-from}夕方[ゆうがた]六時[ろくじ]{まで|made-until}バス{が|ga-subject}走[はし]ります。
en: Buses run from nine in the morning until six in the evening.
why: The time something starts takes から.

jp: 毎日[まいにち]夜[よる]十二時[じゅうにじ]{まで|made-until}電車[でんしゃ]{が/は|ga-existence}あります。
en: There are trains until midnight every day.
why: まで marks the time up to which something continues.

jp: その切符[きっぷ]{は|wa-topic}私[わたし]{の|no-pronoun}です。
en: That ticket is mine.
why: の can stand in for a noun that is understood, giving mine.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-topic}電車[でんしゃ]{が|ga-stative}大好[だいす]きです。
en: My younger brother loves trains.
why: The thing liked with 好き is marked with が.

jp: 駅[えき]{に|ni-location}銀行[ぎんこう]{も|mo-both}郵便局[ゆうびんきょく]{も|mo-both}あります。
en: There are both a bank and a post office at the station.
why: Putting も after each of two nouns means both.

jp: 切符[きっぷ]{と|to-and}パスポート{を|o-object}見[み]せてください。
en: Please show your ticket and passport.
why: と joins two nouns into one list: ticket and passport.

jp: 明日[あした]{は|wa-topic}朝[あさ]早[はや]く駅[えき]{に/へ|ni-destination}来[き]てください。
en: Please come to the station early tomorrow morning.
why: The place you come to is the destination and takes に or へ.

jp: 私[わたし]{は|wa-topic}バス{より|yori-comparison}電車[でんしゃ]{が|ga-stative}好[す]きです。
en: I like trains better than buses.
why: The thing you compare against is marked with より: better than buses.

jp: 毎朝[まいあさ]この橋[はし]{を|o-path}渡[わた]ります。
en: I cross this bridge every morning.
why: The bridge you move across is marked with を.
